# Introducing the deposit return scheme

The long-awaited deposit return scheme (DRS) for aluminium drinks cans and plastic bottles is due to come into being in England, Scotland and Northern Ireland in autumn 2027 but what is it and what difference will it make?

The long-awaited deposit return scheme (DRS) for aluminium drinks cans and plastic bottles is due to come into being in England, Scotland and Northern Ireland in autumn 2027 but what is it and what difference will it make?

![Boy using DRS Machine](/sites/default/files/styles/webp/public/2025-11/shutterstock_2541486063.jpg.webp?itok=GnSGZ95N)

The deposit return scheme is our chance to tackle the drinks litter that makes up more than 70% of litter by volume in this country, at the same time as dramatically improving recycling - and all without leaving the taxpayer out of pocket.

Estimates suggest that more than eight billion drinks containers are littered, buried or burned across the UK each year and Keep Britain Tidy’s National Litter Survey has demonstrated that, by volume, drinks bottles and cans make up almost three quarters of the litter found on our streets. The vast majority of these will be covered by the deposit return scheme.

![Rubbish bag](/sites/default/files/styles/webp/public/2025-08/Untitled_Artwork%2027.png.webp?itok=SXt5NTHc)
![Graphic illustration of a crumpled plastic bottle](/sites/default/files/styles/webp/public/2025-11/Crumpled%20Bottle%20Illustration%20Graphic.png.webp?itok=J_lJpmOX)
![Thumbs up graphic](/sites/default/files/styles/webp/public/2025-11/Thumbs%20up%20icon.png.webp?itok=Tez4JCp1)

The ground-breaking change will have a major impact on the drinks packaging we use every day and the amount of that packaging that is littered. Along with [Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR)](/extended-producer-responsibility) reforms, DRS has huge potential to address the litter crisis and create a more circular economy, meaning that valuable materials are retrieved and recycled rather than ending up in landfill or being burned in energy-from-waste plants.

It’s a disgrace that, for so long, we have polluting our environment with litter that is in fact a valuable and scarce resources that we should be capturing and recycling.

No other policy can boost recycling of a product to above 90% and reduce its littering by 85%, all with industry enthusiastically supporting it and agreeing to fund it.

Evidence from more than 40 other countries and regions around the world shows that these schemes work and suggest that, if we get DRS right, we should see collection rates for drink containers increase to well above 90%, producing clean material for recycling and preventing them from littering our streets and polluting our waterways and, ultimately, our oceans.

#### How will it work?

A deposit return scheme involves paying a small deposit when purchasing a drink in a plastic or aluminium container.

This will be refunded through the customer's choice of cash, card or a voucher when the container is taken back to a return point.

It does not equate to an increase in the price of the drink itself as the deposit is fully refundable.

#### When is DRS set to launch?

DRS is due to be introduced in October 2027 and this timeline must be adhered to by industry and retailers.

#### Is glass in the DRS?

Glass will not be included in DRS at its launch in October 2027.

This means that the millions of glass bottles that are littered in the UK will continue to cause harm to people, pets and wildlife, and precious resources will continue to be wasted.

Keep Britain Tidy campaigned for the inclusion of glass in DRS but the decision was taken by government to exclude the material.

#### How is DRS going to be funded?

DRS will be funded by drinks producers who will provide return points (mostly situated in retailers) with a handling fee for each container they collect.

# How to enter

Nominating your company for an award can be a daunting experience if you've never done it before, but fortunately the entry process for the National Sustainability Awards could not be simpler - here's how it works:  
  
**Who can enter the awards?**  
 The awards are open to any relevant organisation or individual based in the UK. Please note we will require contact details for the company nominated and not PR contact details.

**Choose your categories**  
 There are 23 categories to choose from. You can enter as many categories as you like, submitting each entry separately via the online form. Visit the [categories page](categories.php) to read the criteria.

**Write a brief company profile**  
 Tell us about your organisation in 150 words or less. Your profile should give an overview of the company itself rather than the specific product, project or service, and may be used publicly in awards marketing material.

**Write a brief synopsis of your entry**  
In 150 words or less, briefly summarise your entry. This will be included in the awards brochure should you be shortlisted.

**Write your main entry**  
 Your nomination will be judged on a supporting statement of no more than 1000 words.

**Submit your nomination online via the [entry form](entry_form.php)**  
 Upload all your documents (preferably in Word or PDF format) to the entry form and add your contact details (including your UK office address) so we can confirm that we've received your entry. Please note that there is a maximum 4mb size limit per file and our system may be unable to process your entry if you exceed this limit.

**Don't forget your logo!**  
 A large, high quality company logo must be uploaded with each submission - if you're nominating multiple companies for the same award please provide all relevant logos.

**How much does it cost to enter the awards?**  
 Nothing! The awards are completely free to enter.

**I've entered and received a confirmation email - what happens next?**  
 Soon after the awards close for entries, we will announce the shortlist, from which our judging panel will select the winners who will be announced at The London Marriott Hotel, Grosvenor Square on 8 October 2026. The shortlist will be published on our website and all shortlist entrants will be notified by email.

**Read our guide to [creating an awards entry](https://perspectivepublishing.co.uk/dev/cms/uploads/pdf/creating_an__awards__entry.pdf)  
 Read our [example awards entry](https://perspectivepublishing.co.uk/dev/cms/uploads/pdf/example_entry.pdf)**

**TERMS & CONDITIONS:**  
 • Firms can enter more than one category.  
 • Firms are encouraged to nominate themselves.  
 • The award winners will be chosen by an extensive panel of INDEPENDENT expert judges, using a fair and transparent judging process.  
 • Additional material will not be accepted.  
 • A clear timeframe must be stated in the submission. The project should have been launched or come to fruition in the last 18 months.  
 • Judges may not participate in those categories where there are conflicts of interest.

**WHY ENTER?**  
 • Stand out against the competition

  17th APRIL 2027 | NEW DELHI, INDIA

## The Awards

Global Environment Awards organised by the Energy And Environment Foundation shall recognize outstanding contribution by the individuals, team, unit, region / project organization and honour them for their excellent contributions, commitment and actions that have made a positive impact on the environment. Whether by helping to improve the management of natural resources, demonstrating new ways to tackle climate change or raising awareness of emerging environmental challenges, Global Sustainability Award serve as an inspiration for the transformative action, business excellence and environment management across the world.

## Focus

»   Sustainability Management  
 »   Sustainable Business Strategy / Practices  
 »   Green Initiatives and production optimization  
 »   Health Safety & Environment Practices and Performance  
 »   Sustainability Practices: Social, Economic, Ecology and Environmental  
 »   Developing, Improving and Sustaining a Clean and Green Environment  
 »   Creating an Inspiring Ecosystem  
 »   Sustainable City: Urban Solutions  
 »   Sustainable Transport Systems  
 »   Innovative Water Solutions  
 »   Energy And Environmentally Efficient Plant Operations  
 »   Environmental Efficiency. Energy Efficiency, E-waste Recycling  
 »   Renewable Energy for Sustainable Development

## Objectives

Encourage & motivate to adopt best practices and become role model for others to emulate. Encourage implementation of strategies for improvement in operation standards. It gives morale boost to management, concerned team, employees and all stakeholders.

## Eligibility

These Awards are open for Nomination to all Large, Medium, Small Scale Industrial / Service Sector Companies / Organizations and their regions / Units, projects. Academic Institutions are eligible for participation in the award.

## Application

EEnergy And Environment Foundation Global Award’s Application Form and Rules & Regulations can be obtained by sending request by email to [dranilgarg2024@gmail.com](mailto:dranilgarg2024@gmail.com).  
 For details visit [www.ee-foundation.org](https://ee-foundation.org/).  
 Evaluation of nominations for Global Sustainability Awards is an intensive process. Nominations are evaluated by the Jury - experts from Government, Academia and Industry.

## Submission of Application

Global Sustainability Award’s application complete with all information and documents alongwith applicable processing fee should be reach Secretariat in soft (MS world file) and hard form (printed copy by post) on or before **May 15, 2027.**

## Selection Process

»   Preliminary evaluation of nominations.  
 »   Mandatory Oral Presentation with original documents by all short-listed nominee company/units in presence of Jury members constituted by Energy And Environment Foundation.   
 »   Site visit of short-listed companies / units.

## Nomination Form

What is the Times Now Global Sustainability Alliance – ESG Impact Summit?

The ESG Impact Summit serves as a pivotal platform to unite thought leaders, industry experts, policymakers, and practitioners in exploring the critical roles of CSR and ESG frameworks to create action and impact.

The summit will shine a spotlight on exemplary organizations, foundations and more leading the charge in sustainability. Through standalone addresses, fireside chats, and roundtable discussions, attendees will delve into the success stories of the impact creators—referred to as ‘Paladins’—and discuss why readiness for Net Zero emissions and robust ESG goals is urgent.

What is the purpose of this nomination?

This nomination process aims to identify and recognize companies demonstrating exceptional commitment to Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) and Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) practices, specifically focusing on tangible outcomes and alignment with business objectives. We seek to showcase organizations integrating ESG into their core business strategies for measurable positive impact.

Who is eligible to apply?

Any firm registered under the laws of India and have business operations in India can apply for the nomination in the Award, either directly or through an Agency.

How do I enter?

Please visit our website to register on the platform and begin preparing your entry online using the online entry system.

Please be mindful of the word limits for each segment.

Is the information we submit safe?

Yes, all submissions will be treated with the highest level of confidentiality. We ensure that no information provided will be disclosed to anyone outside of the research partner. To further safeguard your data, research partner is required to sign a strict confidentiality agreement before they are granted access to any of the entries, ensuring that your information remains secure and private.

When is the entry deadline?

30th November

When will the winners be announced?

12th December 2024

## ABOUT CII 4R (REDUCE, REUSE, RECYCLE, REPAIR) AWARD

## Excellence in Waste Management

### Background

The Confederation of Indian Industry (CII) is pleased to announce the 7th edition of the 4R Awards 2026, which recognize and celebrate sustainable practices across industries and academic institutions. The 4R Awards embody the evolving understanding of sustainability, promoting a holistic approach to waste and resource management.

These awards honor organizations that are leading the way in sustainable waste management. By highlighting efforts in waste reduction, recycling, reuse, and repair, the 4R Awards shine a spotlight on companies making significant contributions to environmental conservation, economic growth, and societal well-being.

CII’s initiative underscores the growing recognition of the vital role waste management plays in protecting the environment, safeguarding public health, and fostering sustainable business practices. The 7th edition of the 4R Awards continues to inspire industries to innovate, adopt cleaner technologies, and work toward minimizing their environmental impact.

### Objectives

Promote Sustainable Waste Management Practices : Encourage industries, start-ups, and academic institutions to adopt and scale sustainable waste management practices anchored in the principles of Reduce, Reuse, Recycle, and Repair (4R).

Recognize Leadership in Sustainability : Honour organizations, institutions, and individuals demonstrating exemplary leadership and measurable impact in advancing sustainable and responsible waste management.

Advance the Circular Economy : Support the transition to a circular economy by recognizing innovative approaches that minimize waste generation, enhance resource efficiency, and extend product lifecycles through reuse and repair.

Inspire Innovation and Best Practices : Promote the development and adoption of cleaner technologies, breakthrough innovations, and best practices that drive waste reduction and resource conservation.

Encourage Multi-Stakeholder Collaboration : Foster collaboration among industry, academia, start-ups, and government bodies to accelerate the adoption of sustainable practices and build a shared vision for a cleaner and greener future.

Raise Awareness and Drive Behavioural Change : Increase awareness of the critical role of sustainable waste management in environmental protection, public health, and inclusive economic growth, while inspiring action-oriented change.

Align with the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) :  Contribute to global sustainability efforts by aligning with the UN Sustainable Development Goals, particularly SDG 12: Responsible Consumption and Production, which underpins environmental conservation, climate action, economic growth, and social well-being.

### CII 4R Awards 2026

#### All the large industries, MSMEs and start-ups across the sectors and also the research labs / Academic Institutions can apply for the categories below:

### CII 4 Awards 2026 Categories

* Excellence in Managing Municipal Solid Waste by private firms
* Excellence in Innovative Solutions by Start-ups for Sustainable Waste Management
* Excellence in 4R by Industry (Managing own waste): Manufacturing and service sector
* Excellence in developing the zero / minimum waste products
* Excellence in Best Practices managing plastics and packaging wastes (Including PIBOs/PROs/Recyclers/Co-processors)
* Excellence in Best Practices managing E-waste (Including PROs, Recyclers / processors)
* Excellence in Innovation Solutions / technology by Research Labs /Academic Institutes for Sustainable Waste Management

## Who Can Apply / Why To Apply / How To Apply / Recognition Process

### Who Can Apply?

**1. All the Companies/firms registered in India in the following categories:**

- Large Enterprises
- Medium/ Small/ Micro Enterprises
- Start-up
- R&D Institute
- Academic Institute

  

Manufacturing\* & Services\* | Investment # | Turnover || Micro Enterprises | Up to 1 cr. | Less than 5 cr. |
| Small Enterprises | Up to 10 cr. | Less than 50 cr. |
| Medium Enterprises | Up to 20 cr. | Less than 100 cr. |
| Large Enterprises | Above 20 cr. | Above 100 cr. |

**Note:**   
*\*Enterprises engaged in the manufacture or production, processing or preservation of goods. Investment in plant and machinery is the original cost excluding land and building and the items specified by the Ministry of Small-Scale Industries vide its notification No.S.O.1722(E) dated October 5, 2006.*  
*\*\*Enterprises engaged in providing or rendering of services and whose investment in equipment (original cost excluding land and building, and furniture, fittings and other items not directly related to the service rendered or as may be notified under the MSMED Act, 2006)*

**2. All the Companies**

1. Providing services in managing MSW such as collection & transportation, processing/ recovery and scientific disposal including landfill management.
2. Managing wastes generated in from their industrial activities; their own activities by adopting best waste management practices, 4R practices and through disposal system.
3. Producing products which generate minimum/zero waste or lead to no waste
4. Sells or import any plastics and packaging items and electronic commodity/ or engaged in production of plastic raw material to be used as raw material or generate electronic items /or responsibility for collection and channelization of these waste, and recyclers.

**3. Start-ups incorporated or registered in India with following criteria:**

1. Up to a period of ten years from the date of incorporation/registration.
2. Annual turnover not exceeding Rs 25 crore in any preceding financial year, and
3. If it works towards innovation, development or improvement of products or processes or services, or if it's a scalable business model with a high potential of employment generation or wealth creation
4. Start-ups which are offering innovative solutions for sustainable waste management.

content:
#### Background

The CII Young 4R Awards 2025 aim to recognize and celebrate forward-thinking institutions that foster youth-led innovation in waste management. Focused on the principles of the circular economy—**Reduce, Reuse, Recycle, Repair**. This national-level award provides a platform to young minds to showcase transformative solutions that address India’s most pressing waste challenges. Through this initiative, we aim to inspire scalable and sustainable innovations that contribute to a cleaner, more resource-efficient future.

#### Highlights

Recognizing student-driven innovations in waste management.

Focus on circular economy principles: Reduce, Reuse, Recycle, Repair.

Opportunity to gain national visibility and CII recognition.

Prizes, mentorship opportunities, and certification for all participants.

#### Categories

* There will be total 3 Awards in different categories.
* Top 10 shortlisted participants receive a Certificate of Merit.

#### Evaluation Process

Step 1 – Online registration on CII Waste to Worth website ([www.ciiwaste2worth.com](http://www.ciiwaste2worth.com))

Step 2 – Online Submission of Application

Step 3 – Jury Evaluation

Step 4 – Announcement of Winners

#### Eligibility Criteria

**Age Limit:** Applicants must be under 35 years of age at the time of application submission.

**Who Can Apply:**

* Undergraduate, postgraduate and PhD students enrolled in full-time programs.
* Fresh graduates actively working on waste management innovations.
* Applicants must be affiliated with recognized institutions or waste research labs in India.

**Project Type:**

* Submissions can be individual or team projects.
* The solution must be focused on waste management, circular economy, or resource efficiency.

**Institutional Endorsement:**

* The submitted solution must be certified by the affiliated institution or supervising authority.

#### Why Participate?

**All Participants Receive:**

* Participation Certificate from CII
* Acknowledgment in CII publications
* Invitation to attend the CII Symposium on Waste to Worth Technologies

* Trophy & Certificate presented during the award ceremony
* Featured coverage in CII publications and major media platforms
* Opportunities for future collaboration with industry leaders and investors

#### How To Apply

1. Register online: **[[CII Young 4R Award 2025](https://forms.mycii.in/form/0913238a-7b48-4c60-8cc1-2c33bdfb6a6a)]**
2. Submit filled application form with supporting documents
3. Upload relevant documents while submitting the application
4. Submit the completed application by the deadline

#### Application Fees

* No application fee for institutions under the Institute/University Innovations category.
* Participation is completely free to encourage maximum innovation and inclusivity.

#### Jury

The evaluation will be conducted by a distinguished jury.

#### Schedule

| Milestone | Date |
| --- | --- |
| Announcement of Awards | 4th November 2025 |
| Submission Deadline | 31st March 2026 |
| Jury Evaluation & Shortlisting | April /May 2026 |
| Results & Award Ceremony | 8th June 2026 |

Confederation of Indian Industry (CII) is organizing a Mission on Waste to Worth Technologies to Singapore from 19th – 23rd May 2025 to enhance India’s competitiveness by exploring advanced waste management technologies. This mission will provide exposure to best practices in waste management and foster collaboration between India and Singapore.

The mission will include representatives from industry, start-ups, law firms, academic institutions, and more. Participants will meet key government, academic, and industry leaders, and visit various waste management facilities and innovation centres.

A couple of visits to Environmental Resource Institutes, Singapore Sustainability Academy, Singapore Waste Management & Recycling Association as well as visit to few Incineration Plants of top Singapore companies and facilities are also being planned. List of the tentative organisation will be visited is mentioned below-

Tuas Incineration Plant (Waste-to-Energy)  
 SembWaste (Singapore’s Waste Management Services Provider)  
 The Singapore Sustainability Academy  
 Environmental Resource Institutes (e.g., NUS or NTU)  
 Hitachi Zosen Corporation (Singapore)  
 Blue Planet Plant Visit  
 Singapore Waste Management Association  
 Singapore Society of Material Cycles and Waste Management  
 Singapore Waste Research Foundation

# CII Waste & Resource Management Summit 2025

#### 11-12 September 2025

Register Now

**About the Summit**

India's rapid urbanization and industrialization have led to increased consumption of natural resources and significant waste generation. Recognizing the environmental challenges posed by these developments, the summit aimed to address effective waste management strategies and resource conservation. It served as a platform to explore the latest concepts and emerging technologies in the waste management sector, facilitating business-to-business interactions and knowledge dissemination among industry stakeholders.

**Schedule:**

*   Day 1 - 11 Sep 2025 : Presentations from the Shortlisted projects - CII National Award for Environmental Best Practices 2025
*   Day 2 - 12 Sep 2025 : Inaugural Session and Technical Sessions of CII Waste & Resource Management Summit 2025

**Key Objectives**

*   Promote the concepts of circular economy, waste management, and resource conservation.
*   Explore emerging technologies and best practices in waste management.
*   Facilitate business interactions to encourage technology adoption.
*   Disseminate knowledge and build capacity among industries on waste management and resource conservation

**Focus Areas**

*   Strategies for resource-efficient growth of Indian industry.

## Sarata Chandra Panigrahi Memorial National Award on Sustainability

Late Sarata Chandra Panigrahi, a *Gandhian Socialist* and *Environmentalist*, worked throughout his life for the social, environmental, economic and cultural uplift-ment of down trodden and the weaker sections of people of the backward KBK region of Odisha. Late Panigrahi, who was born in April 1922, had served the nation by joining *Indian Army* and rendering war services, during the *Second World War* as a Superintendent Engineer (SE) of *Military Engineering Services (MES)*, under *Eastern Commands* of Government of India. He is well known for his unprecedented dedications and tireless struggle for more than a half century in *“Bhudan Jagnya (Land Reforms) Movements”* and *Praja Andolan*“ of the State, being inspired by than Vinoba Bhabe, Jaiprakash Narayan and Ram Monohar Lohia - is well recognized, who has created history by distributing the *Jagiri* and all other types of Land, in his life span to more than 2 lakhs plus landless, poor and marginalized *Adivasis & Harijans*, providing them the minimum livelihood security for sustaining their basics, especially in the neglected *Gadajat* Regions. He along with 18 thousand *Harijans and Adivasis*, went on a Public Protest and Procession and tore the Lower Court *Stay Orders*, issued by the District Judge, asking *Harijans and Adivasis*, not to enter their *Jagiri Land*, being bribed by *Gountias (Land Lords)*, Who lost half acre of their land because the Land Reform Movement, in a Public Meeting, hence Late Sarata Chandra faced Contempt of the Court. He was a dedicated worker for the *Sarvadaya Movement* in Odisha with Late Gopabandhu Choudhary and Malati Choudhary. He was the Founder and President of *Harijan Adivasi Sammilani*, at Balangir, since 1946, with an enrolled membership of more than 75 thousand and was running this trust, with his own expenses for about 58 long years till his death, to safeguard the interests of these vulnerable communities, being inspired by Mahatma Gandhi, Father of the Nation.   
  
 Late Panigrahi is known for his immense contribution for up-holding our age-old high moral value system of the Society. His principle of life was – *“I desire not the kingdom of heaven, if it does not come through the path of righteousness”*. He has refused an Offer, by than Chief Minister of Odisha, *Late Nandini Satpathy*, to become a Member of *Upper House (Rajya Shabha)* of the Indian Parliament, on moral ground. Moreover, He was instrumental in delivering many public works like, establishing major educational and cultural institutions of the region, like, Women’s College, Town Girl’s High School, Town High School, Ayurved College, Sanskrit College etc and most remarkably he has contributed to *Girl’s education* and *Women Empowerment*. In addition, His dedication and historic role in the restoration of pre-independence period’s re-knowned *Cultural Institution* of Western-Odisha called *Koshola Kala Mandal* is well recalled.

# How to enter

Nominating your company for an award can be a daunting experience if you've never done it before, but fortunately the entry process for the National Sustainability Awards could not be simpler - here's how it works:  
  
**Who can enter the awards?**  
 The awards are open to any relevant organisation or individual based in the UK. Please note we will require contact details for the company nominated and not PR contact details.

**Choose your categories**  
 There are 23 categories to choose from. You can enter as many categories as you like, submitting each entry separately via the online form. Visit the [categories page](categories.php) to read the criteria.

**Write a brief company profile**  
 Tell us about your organisation in 150 words or less. Your profile should give an overview of the company itself rather than the specific product, project or service, and may be used publicly in awards marketing material.

**Write a brief synopsis of your entry**  
In 150 words or less, briefly summarise your entry. This will be included in the awards brochure should you be shortlisted.

**Write your main entry**  
 Your nomination will be judged on a supporting statement of no more than 1000 words.

**Submit your nomination online via the [entry form](entry_form.php)**  
 Upload all your documents (preferably in Word or PDF format) to the entry form and add your contact details (including your UK office address) so we can confirm that we've received your entry. Please note that there is a maximum 4mb size limit per file and our system may be unable to process your entry if you exceed this limit.

**Don't forget your logo!**  
 A large, high quality company logo must be uploaded with each submission - if you're nominating multiple companies for the same award please provide all relevant logos.

**How much does it cost to enter the awards?**  
 Nothing! The awards are completely free to enter.

**I've entered and received a confirmation email - what happens next?**  
 Soon after the awards close for entries, we will announce the shortlist, from which our judging panel will select the winners who will be announced at The London Marriott Hotel, Grosvenor Square on 8 October 2026. The shortlist will be published on our website and all shortlist entrants will be notified by email.

 Read our [example awards entry](https://perspectivepublishing.co.uk/dev/cms/uploads/pdf/example_entry.pdf)**

 • Firms are encouraged to nominate themselves.  
 • The award winners will be chosen by an extensive panel of INDEPENDENT expert judges, using a fair and transparent judging process.  
 • Additional material will not be accepted.  
 • A clear timeframe must be stated in the submission. The project should have been launched or come to fruition in the last 18 months.  
 • Judges may not participate in those categories where there are conflicts of interest.

**WHY ENTER?**

# IISD wins big in global Think Tank Awards

IISD brought home three top honours at the prestigious 2019 Think Tank Awards, presented by Prospect Magazine. The accolades include 2019’s Think Tank to Watch, given to an innovative think tank that is “on the move.”

Winnipeg, July 17, 2019 – The International Institute for Sustainable Development (IISD) brought home three top honours at the 2019 Think Tank Awards, presented by [Prospect Magazine](https://www.prospectmagazine.co.uk/). The accolades include 2019’s Think Tank to Watch, given to an innovative think tank “on the move.”

The ceremony took place in the Churchill Room at the Houses of Parliament in London, England, on July 17. The prestigious annual awards recognize the “most original, inﬂuential and rigorous work” of think tanks around the world. This is only the second time a Canadian institution has won in the competition.

Focused on the most pressing challenges facing people, governments and businesses, the awards feature work in four categories: Economic and Financial Affairs; Foreign Affairs; Science, Health, Environment and Energy; and Social Policy. Awards are given separately to organizations in the United Kingdom, the European Union, and the United States and the rest of the world.

IISD was shortlisted in three of the four categories, up against highly distinguished organizations in the United States and rest of the world, including Carnegie Endowment for International Peace, Peterson Institute for International Economics and RAND Corporation.

A Winnipeg-based independent think tank, IISD won the Foreign Affairs category, for a report that showed judges from the United Nation’s high court were taking paid work to settle investment treaty disputes between corporations and governments. This had the potential of threatening the independence and impartiality of the world’s top court, and the research ultimately led the court to rethink its practice.

IISD also took the award in the Science, Health, Environment and Energy category, for research into how increasing demand for minerals and metals for green technologies such as wind and solar could affect fragile but resource-rich countries.

An independent panel of judges, chaired by Prospect Magazine’s editor, Tom Clark, looked for evidence of inﬂuence on policy and public discourse. The organizers noted that special care was taken to consider both the quality of research and the potential of younger and smaller organizations.

“We have a long history of producing high-quality, impactful work, and these awards are a recognition of the difference an organization like IISD can make,” said acting President and CEO Jane McDonald. “We’re very proud to see our work acknowledged this way, especially by the very high-profile judges on this year’s panel.”

The closure of the Strait of Hormuz cut off roughly 25% of the world’s seaborne oil and 20% of LNG trade. The International Institute for Sustainable Development (IISD) is an award-winning independent think tank working to create a world where people and the planet thrive.

[About IISD](/mission-and-goals "About IISD")

# 21st CII-ITC Sustainability Awards 2026

Application of Intent  
Now Open!

[Apply Now](https://sustainablecompanies.in/awards)

![CII-ITC Sustainability Awards Trophy](awards-2026/image69.svg)

## About the Awards

Instituted in **2006**, the CII-ITC Sustainability Awards recognise and reward excellence in businesses that are seeking ways to be more sustainable and inclusive in their activities. The winners of the Awards are role models that inspire others to follow suit. The Awards are a part of the continued efforts of CESD to create awareness on sustainability practices and to create capacities in business. CII-ITC Sustainability Awards define the science of sustainability performance. Excellence in sustainability is a journey of continuous improvement in processes and results.

In the past 20 years, cumulatively, **1400+** businesses have applied, of which **500+** have been recognised.

The CII-ITC Sustainability Award is the most credible sustainability Award in the country. This Award is meant to be earned.

[Apply Now](https://sustainablecompanies.in/awards) [Journey of Awards](https://sustainabledevelopment.in/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/itc-awards.mp4)

To access brochure write to us at [sustainabilityawards@cii.in](mailto:sustainabilityawards@cii.in)

## Uniqueness of the Awards

Over a period of six months, applicants undergo a rigorous assessment process based on Business Excellence model tailored for business in India. A team of CII-certified Sustainability Assessors spend nearly **1,000 man-hours** per application. A detailed Feedback Report to every applicant is provided to help the organisations get insights to improve their sustainability performance.

#### EFQM Excellence Framework

Uniquely based on EFQM Excellence Framework, designed for those who strive effortlessly to make sustainability their business.

#### Third Party Assured

The only third-party assured Awards in terms of technology, governance, methodology and process.

#### Track Record

In the past 20 years, cumulatively, **1400+** businesses from manufacturing, services and MSMEs sectors have applied, of which **500+** have been recognised so far.

#### Carbon Neutral

The CII-ITC Sustainability Awards is carbon neutral, offset by investing in Gold Standard carbon credit from improved cookstoves project installed in rural India.

## You Should Apply Because

You want to **assess your sustainability performance** based on the Business Excellence Model.

You want to get **strategic insights and identify improvement areas** based on comprehensive and rigorous assessment by independent CII-certified Sustainability Assessors.

**Positions your organisation** as a responsible, future-ready organisation aligned with national and global sustainability standards.

You want to be **recognised as Excellent** in Sustainable Business by the most credible Sustainability Awards in the country.

## Eligibility Criteria

Operating in **India**, for at least **Five Years**

A **Large, Medium, Small, Micro-sized Enterprise** or Independent Unit/Division

From **Manufacturing** or **Service Sector**

## What is ICEF?

The annual India Circular Economy Forum (ICEF) serves as a platform where India’s leading circular economy solutions are presented.

ICEF2026 will bring together experts from industry, startups, academia and policymakers to share the focussed action plan and strategies to implement circularity within their industry. The forum will provide actionable insights and strategies for businesses to meet their environmental compliances and improve their ESG and circularity score while identifying potential growth opportunities. Through expert panels, workshops, and networking opportunities, the forum will foster collaborations and promote policy dialogues that enable the Indian economy to thrive in a sustainable, circular framework.

As the **World Circular Economy Forum (WCEF)** comes to India this September, the Embassy and Sitra are convening a series of roadshows across the country in the lead-up to the global event. The second day at ICEF20206 has been curated in collaboration with WCEF as a precursor roadshow that will inform the upcoming WCEF discussions. A special B2B Networking session will catalyze partnerships and investments between Indian and Finnish companies.

Commencing in 2022, the first 4 editions in 2022-25 successfully convened an illustrious ensemble of thought leaders from industry, heads of state and government, scholars, corporate representatives, youth groups, non-profit organizations, and civil society from across the globe, earning recognition of a responsible and impactful platform, mobilizing opinion-makers to address paramount issues related to sustainable development, resource efficiency, and climate change.

## Unlock game-changing partnerships at ICEF2026!

The entire second day is your exclusive passport to high-powered, face-to-face B2B matchmaking with pioneering Finnish companies. If you are ready to scale your business, launch massive collaborations, or co-create the future with global leaders in innovation, this is where you need to be.

Don’t just watch the industry evolve—be the one driving it forward. Secure your spot at the ICEF2026 B2B discussions and connect with your next major international partner!

Have you achieved outstanding results by implementing circular practices in your company or organisation? Did you design a product that focuses on resource efficiency, longevity and reparability? Are you bringing the circular economy closer to your community by publicly advocating for it and starting initiatives yourself?

![](https://wbcirculareconomy.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/CE-awards-tab-min.png "CE awards tab-min")

Launched in 2025, the Circular Economy Awards became the first regional programme created to recognise and celebrate pioneers, innovators, and changemakers advancing circular economy solutions across the region. The Awards honour outstanding achievements in implementing circular initiatives, projects, products, services, and business models that contribute to sustainable resource use and circular transformation. The Awards recognise stakeholders across seven different categories, showcasing inspiring examples of circular innovation and leadership from across the Western Balkans.

# Global Circular Economy Forum and Awards Ceremony

![Circular economy in action - 2nd forum and award ceremony](/platform/sites/default/files/styles/large/public/screenshot_2026-02-05_154203.png?itok=CGbHbT9d)

The Global Circular Economy Forum and Awards Ceremony will bring together circular economy leaders, pioneers, practitioners, explorers and researchers across industries and supply chains to celebrate circularity. It will focus on implementation, action and impact and participants will share opportunities, good practices, real-life cases and lessons learned from implementing the circular economy.

There will be keynote speeches, panel discussions, workshops and networking opportunities.

Dr Janez Potonick, Co-Chair of the International Resource Panel, UNEP and former European Commissioner for Environment, will give a keynote speech on **resource management** and circular economy and Chrysostomos Adamides will talk about how **hotels in Cyprus** are shifting towards circularity.

There will also be discussions on **maximizing return on investment in the circular economy, how circularity can reduce plastic pollution, how AI can enable the circular economy, the need to embed circular economy principles at the design stage and how organisations can adopt circular economy practices, principles and ISO 59000 Standards**.

# Driving Sustainable Excellence and Corporate Stewardship

Since 2018, the Global Corporate Sustainability Awards (GCSA) have celebrated organizations driving excellence in sustainability across environmental, social, and economic dimensions. These forward-thinking companies align their strategies with global standards like the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and demonstrate commitment to transparency, collaboration, and long-term impact in their industries and communities.

GCSA features two award categories: the Sustainability Reporting Award and the Best Practices Award. Winners are selected by a distinguished panel of experts from business, academic institutions, governments, and NGOs worldwide. They are honored at the annual Global Corporate Sustainability Forum (GCSF), where leaders from over 20 countries convene to exchange insights and drive sustainability forward.

![](https://www.genevaenvironmentnetwork.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/Untitled-design-2025-12-10T153631.874-aspect-ratio-2000-1200-300x180.jpg) 

Last updated: 08 Jun 2026

[Science](https://www.genevaenvironmentnetwork.org/environment-geneva/key-areas-sdg/key-areas/science/) | [Climate](https://www.genevaenvironmentnetwork.org/environment-geneva/key-areas-sdg/key-areas/climate/) | [Nature](https://www.genevaenvironmentnetwork.org/environment-geneva/key-areas-sdg/key-areas/nature/) | [Chemicals and Pollution](https://www.genevaenvironmentnetwork.org/environment-geneva/key-areas-sdg/key-areas/chemicals-pollution/)

Every year, a series of international awards and prizes underscore the growing momentum of global efforts to protect the planet, advance scientific innovation, and strengthen environmental governance. Find here an overview of global flagship awards, thematic environmental prizes, and Swiss-based awards recognizing the champions working towards a healthier, more resilient and just planet.

## Environmental Awards and Prizes

Environmental awards and prizes play a central role in recognizing and amplifying the work of individuals and institutions shaping a more sustainable future. These awards celebrate achievements across diplomacy, science, youth engagement, innovation, and environmental justice while reminding the world of the urgent need for collective action in addressing the interconnected crises of climate change, biodiversity loss, and pollution.

## Global Flagship Environmental Awards

*Recognizing broad, cross-cutting contributions to environmental protection, sustainability, and environmental leadership.*

### UNEP Champions of the Earth

Considered the UN’s highest environmental honor, the Champions of the Earth Award has been given annually since 2005. Through this award, UNEP honors individuals and organizations working on innovative and sustainable solutions to address the triple planetary crisis of climate change, nature and biodiversity loss, and pollution and waste.

The 2026 [nominations](https://www.unep.org/championsofearth/#:~:text=UNEP%20has%20opened%20nominations%20for%20the%202026%20Champions%20of%20the%20Earth%20award%20%E2%80%93%20the%20UN%E2%80%99s%20highest%20environmental%20honour%20%E2%80%93%20this%20year%20focusing%20on%20leaders%20at%20the%20forefront%20of%20caring%20for%20the%20ocean%2C%20an%20ecosystem%20essential%20to%20life%20on%20Earth%20that%20is%20increasingly%20under%20strain.) deadline was **15 April 2026.** This year the award is seeking individuals, organizations, and governments at the forefront of protecting and restoring **ocean** health.

In 2025, UNEP sought nominations from individuals and organizations whose work strengthens climate resilience and contributes to mitigation solutions. The [2025 Champions of the Earth](https://www.unep.org/championsofearth/), announced on 10 December at the 7th UN Environment Assembly, highlight bold climate and environmental action across the awards’ five categories.

* [**Science & Innovation**](https://www.unep.org/championsofearth/award/science-and-innovation): [Imazon (Brazil)](https://www.unep.org/championsofearth/laureates/2025/imazon) – a non-profit research institute which has developed AI deforestation prediction models that inform and help law enforcement protect the Amazon rainforest, while promoting sustainable economic growth.
* [**Lifetime Achievement**](https://www.unep.org/championsofearth/award/lifetime-achievement): [Manfredi Caltagirone](https://www.unep.org/championsofearth/laureates/2025/imazon) (posthumous) – Former head of UNEP’s International Methane Emissions Observatory, Mr. Caltagirone championed transparency and science-based action on me

# Funding Opportunities

The U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) makes funding available through competitive *notice of funding opportunities (NOFOs)*, published on [Grants.gov](https://www.grants.gov/) and the [CMEI Exchange](https://eere-exchange.energy.gov/).

Securing project funding is critical to the success of Clean Cities and Communities efforts to implement alternative fuels, advanced vehicle technologies, and fuel-saving strategies. Funding opportunities are available from many sources inside and outside DOE.

DOE's TTO has awarded more than $570 million through the Technology Integration Program to fund hundreds of projects across the country that advance deployment of efficient transportation technologies. Clean Cities and Communities stakeholders have played critical roles in the success of these projects. Learn more about [funded projects](/projects/).

## Open Funding Opportunities

Current funding opportunities that may be of interest to Clean Cities and Communities stakeholders, including TTO NOFOs issued by DOE, are listed below when available. To suggest adding a funding opportunity to this list, [contact us](/website-contact/).

*No active funding opportunities are available at this time.*

Connect with a [Clean Cities and Communities coalition](/coalitions/contacts/) for information about current or potential Clean Cities and Communities project partnerships and relevant funding opportunities.

FOAs are also listed on [Grants.gov](https://www.grants.gov/), the portal for numerous grant programs administered by federal government agencies, and the DOE [Office of Critical Minerals and Energy Innovation (CMEI) Exchange](https://eere-exchange.energy.gov/) for all CMEI NOFOs.

[Requests for Information](#requests-for-information) also create an opportunity for Clean Cities and Communities partners to share information that may be used for planning and decision-making purposes, including but not limited to determining potential new areas of focus, funding opportunities, analyses, and organizational frameworks.

### Laws and Incentives

The Alternative Fuels Data Center maintains a comprehensive database of [Federal and State Laws and Incentives](https://afdc.energy.gov/laws/) related to alternative fuels and vehicles, air quality, fuel efficiency, and other transportation-related topics.

## Other Funding Opportunities

Transportation-related funding opportunities from organizations and federal agencies outside of DOE are listed below. Some of the government agencies listed have ongoing funding opportunities available; others issue funding notices periodically or assist in forming partnerships that can provide funding opportunities for transportation-related projects.

### U.S. Department of Transportation

* [Congestion Mitigation and Air Quality Improvement (CMAQ) Program](http://www.fhwa.dot.gov/environment/air_quality/cmaq/): Administered by the Federal Highway Administration and the Federal Transit Administration, CMAQ funds projects and programs that reduce transportation-related emissions and relieve traffic congestion. Funds are distributed locally through [metropolitan planning organizations](https://www.planning.dot.gov/mpo/).
* [Federal Lands Access Program (FLAP)](https://highways.dot.gov/federal-lands/flap): The FLAP was established to improve transportation facilities that provide access to, are adjacent to, or are located within federal lands. The program supplements state and local resources for public roads, transit systems, and other transportation facilities, with an emphasis on high-use recreation sites and economic generators.

# Environmental Grants

Environmental Education & Project Grants

The Solutions Project has dedicated itself to improving the lives and environment of the disenfranchised for years. After nearly a decade of experience, we’ve learned a valuable lesson about funding an environment grant from working with numerous groups on environmental projects. We understand the importance of financing and that your community service has never been more crucial than it is today.

We want to show our support for your vision and are inspired by your commitment to improving the lives of those in your community. If your group is working on issues related to education, community development, environmental involvement, or environmental justice, you can apply for an environment grant below.

*NOTE: The Solutions Project does not handle government grants and the following information is for educational purposes only. If you would like to learn more about the grants that we do offer or learn more about our grantees please visit [our Grantmaking page](https://thesolutionsproject.org/what-we-do/grantmaking/).*

## What is an Environment Grant?

To preserve human health and the environment, The Solutions Project collaborates with state, tribal, and municipal governments and institutions of higher education, non-profit organizations, and other qualifying entities through grants for environmental projects. The Solutions Project’s systematic approach to distributing funding allows us to tap into local expertise vital to achieving its goals. Every year, the Solutions Project distributes grants to its state, tribal, municipal, educational, charitable, and other partners. The Solutions Project’s funding helps maintain state, tribal, and local ties and encourages cutting-edge research, community knowledge, and empowerment in environmental protection. The Solutions Project is committed to investing 95% of its resources in creative frontline leadership of color, with at least 80% of those funds going to women-led organizations.

After receiving an award, the grantee is ready to begin working on the tasks described in the approved grant work plan. Compliance with different grant rules and the terms and conditions mentioned in the grant agreement is essential for a successful grant project. Regulations such as filing federal financial reports, providing progress reports, and restricting lobbying activity are common terms and conditions. Throughout the life of the project, recipients should evaluate the terms and conditions of the environment grant to verify compliance with all requirements.

## What are Environmental Educational Grants?

Grants for environmental education are issued to groups and organizations that are creating initiatives that facilitate learning about environmental concerns, tackle environmental issues, and take measures to improve the environment.

Environmental education includes the following elements:

1. Environmental knowledge, awareness, sensitivity, and understanding concerning current and future challenges
2. Environment-conscious attitudes and drive to enhance or preserve environmental quality
3. Ability to recognize and assist in the resolution of environmental issues
4. Participation in actions that result in environmental challenges being resolved

While environmental education does not promote a certain point of view or action, its aim centers around teaching people how to think critically about environmental issues and improving problem-solving and decision-making abilities.

# **Environmental Conservation in America**

In the vast landscape of environmental conservation, where the stakes are as high as the planet's future, philanthropy plays a pivotal role. Foundations across America are stepping up, providing crucial funding for environmental research programs and charities, but the need for support remains immense. **The Funding Need** The environmental sector faces a dire funding gap. According to data from **FoundationSearch**, a comprehensive database of U.S. foundation grants, environmental causes require billions in funding annually to address issues like climate change, biodiversity loss, and pollution. The urgency of these issues is underscored by the fact that without adequate research and conservation efforts, the impacts of environmental degradation will continue to escalate, affecting not just ecosystems but human health, economies, and global stability. **Who is Impacted by the Lack of Funding?** The lack of sufficient funding impacts a broad spectrum of stakeholders:
  
  
**Researchers and Scientists:** Without funding, cutting-edge research into sustainable practices, renewable energy, and ecological restoration stalls. This delay in innovation can mean missed opportunities for mitigating climate change effects.
  
  
**Local Communities:** Particularly those in vulnerable areas, who face the brunt of environmental degradation through loss of livelihoods, health issues from pollution, and increased vulnerability to natural disasters.
  
  
**Future Generations:** The long-term effects of environmental neglect will be inherited by future generations, who will face a world with diminished natural resources and biodiversity.
  
  
**Wildlife and Ecosystems:** Species extinction rates are accelerating, and ecosystems are collapsing, which in turn affects everything from water purification to carbon sequestration.
  
  
**The Philanthropic Response** Despite the challenges, numerous foundations are actively supporting environmental initiatives:
  
  
**The Bezos Earth Fund** has committed $10 billion by 2030 to fight climate change and protect nature, focusing on transformative projects like electric bus fleets and carbon-absorbing crops.
  
  
**The Doris Duke Charitable Foundation** supports environmental conservation, with a focus on sustainable landscapes and wildlife protection.
  
  
**The Environmental Grantmakers Association** (EGA) represents over 35 years of environmental philanthropy, advocating for equitable and sustainable ecosystems. According to **FoundationSearch**, there are over 2,000 foundations in the U.S. that have given grants for environmental causes in recent years. The average grant size varies widely, but for environmental research, grants can range from small sums of $5,000 to significant investments of over $1 million, depending on the project's scope and the foundation's focus. **Future Trends in Environmental Philanthropy** The future of environmental philanthropy looks promising yet challenging:
  
  
**Increased Focus on Climate Change:** With climate change becoming an undeniable global crisis, more foundations are likely to prioritize funding for climate mitigation and adaptation strategies.
  
  
**Collaborative Funding:** There's a growing trend towards collaborative efforts where multiple foundations pool resources for larger, more impactful projects. This approach not only increases the funding pool but also fosters innovation through shared knowledge and resources.
  
  
**Technology and Innovation:** Foundations are increasingly interested in funding technology-driven solutions, from AI in environmental monitoring to renewable ener
